title: "Tutorial 7 · MLE, MAP & Bayesian Updating"
subtitle: "After L15 · 80 minutes"
---

Estimate a coin bias, update a Beta prior, and see regularization as prior information.

## Part A · Worksheet (~40 min, pen and paper)

### Problem 1 — Bernoulli MLE

For 3 heads and 1 tail, write the likelihood/log-likelihood and derive the MLE.

### Problem 2 — Beta posterior

With prior Beta$(2,2)$, find the posterior after those flips and its mean.

### Problem 3 — MAP

Find the interior MAP of Beta$(5,3)$ and compare it with the mean.

### Problem 4 — Sequential update

Show that updating after batches (2H,1T) then (1H,0T) matches one update with all data.

### Problem 5 — Prior as counts

Interpret Beta$(10,2)$ using pseudo-counts, and explain when data will dominate it.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solutions — open only after attempting everything

**1.** $L(\theta)=\theta^3(1-\theta)$; derivative of log likelihood gives $\hat{\theta}=3/4$.

**2.** Posterior Beta$(5,3)$ with mean $5/8$.

**3.** MAP $(5-1)/(5+3-2)=2/3$; mean is $5/8$.

**4.** Both yield Beta$(5,3)$ because sufficient statistics add.

**5.** The prior contributes 9 head-like and 1 tail-like MAP pseudo-count; enough observations overwhelm fixed prior counts.
:::
